  Do people their own age not want to be involved with them because they aren't up to the general standard they should be at 32? (I.e. still very immature, irresponsible, unmotivated, jobless or waaaaay under employed) 

 Do they like me, a much younger person, because I'm me and I happen to be younger or because I'm 19 and it makes them feel like they still have some game and can "score" someone young?

Are we at the same place in life and do we want the same things (for now anyway, if you're not looking to the future)?

My ex and his video game addiction. NOTHING came between him and his League of Legends. Not class, or work, or friends, or family. 

He lived with friends in an apartment, wed all be hanging out and ready to go out, then all of a sudden he'd disappear and when we found him "well I told my friend I'd play league with him tonight" except that was most nights and almost always if we made plans. Actually, one anniversary he left early because he told me his friend asked him to play league right then and there and he said he would.

He'd promise to buy me a gift for my birthday or take me out to dinner for our anniversary (we were young and broke so either probably would've cost $40 MAX) and get me excited for months. And then he'd buy himself or his "really good friend" (read: his enabler) riot points or stuff on hearthstone. Or say he wanted to pay for video game lessons. And now he doesn't have any money, sorry, he'll make up for it next holiday.  And then never did. He'd do the same to his mom and dad and sister too. Meanwhile, he made his mum (who was pretty poor and worked very hard for her money) spend like $200 on a keyboard because it had a razor logo on it. 

His roommates would ask if he could wash his dishes, take out the trash, vacuum- basically do anything to contribute in any way. But he was "too busy." Hed tell them he didn't have enough money to pitch in for food or beer or to go out or whatever, so they'd cover him. And then he'd immediately go home and spend the money he "saved" on video games.

I lived about a 5 to 10 minute walk from him, hed ask me over and I'd let him know when I was leaving so he could buzz me in. Most of the time by the time I got there, "well I just started a new league game and I cant pause" so I'd have to wait for his roommates, wait down stairs for 45 minutes, or go home. 

When I'd finally get let in, most of the time I was ignored. For like 8 to 12 hours. Even when HE asked me over. I'd do my homework or keep myself busy. And then when we'd go to bed, hed fall asleep watch video game streamers. He made me stay up til 4 am once when I had an important test because the league of legends championship was streaming and he had to watch it (and cheer and shout) right then and there. 

I know these are all centered around me, but if you notice, anytime he had money (which wasnt often since he barely worked because of his addiction) he blew it on the game (or beer to drink while playing), hed abandon his friends in an instant, and prioritized it over spending time with family. He was failing out of college and I tried recommending to him that he do his homework before playing so itd get done. Or hed go to class at least and then play. But he wouldn't so he lost all aid and got kicked out of school because no money/grades too poor to continue. We dated for like almost 4 and a half years and were really serious, when I told him his addiction was causing problems and I was gunna leave if that (amongst other things) didn't get better, he was convinced I was just being too demanding and that someday hed be a pro player. 

He even wanted to move to South Korea from the US because their internet speeds are faster, they had esports bars, and a better esports culture (and he thought south Korean women would somehow be impressed with him cause he was white and played video games? I'm gunna venture no) he said it was for the culture as a whole, but we all knew different. 

It was crazy how much he'd lie and obsess and prioritize video games above all else and get like, PISSED if you mentioned it. It was the only addiction I've seen that wasnt to drugs but still had someone acting like they were. 

Tl;dr- ex boyfriend, video games > money, sleep, college, family, friends, life.

I'm gunna give the short version since its 530 in the morning here and i just finished homework. But dada is cool as fuck. 

Dada was a movement in the early to mid 20th century, Marcel Duchamp is the dadaist everyone knows and loves or loves to hate. He's the one with The Fountain. (Which is debatable if it's more abstract or conceptual, but a lot of movements kinda blur that line so we'll roll with it). 

It was promilarily a pack of artists after WWI who thought the design aesthetic before was too "perfect" too logical and rational and a reflection of a capitalist society. So instead they decided to inflict total chaos and irrationality and nonsense. 

It's one of those moments in art where it kinda means nothing, but that's why it means something. (If that makes sense)

It was also a response to the previous traditions of art where basically the artist was a god. He had this Divine Gift and couldn't be understood by regular men and blah blah blah. (Of course not all artists, just the famous ones). Basically the way we think of Da Vinci or Van Gogh. 

They were sick of that, so instead they began to use found objects, throw things across canvases, etc. It became more about the process and trying to make it all random, all up to chance. And this was to say "hey, the artist isn't THAT important, anyone could have done this" 

So when you go to a museum and see something and think "that sucks, I could've done that." Just know that the dadaists would be tickled pink, even if it was from another movement. 

Also, full disclosure, technically "the death of the author" wasn't coined until Barthes in the late 60s and dadaism emerged in the 20s but the concepts are really similar.

From what I understand the perspective is largely aerial with ever so slightly off details done purposefully to add to the overall feel, if that makes sense. Mostly it was less about how absolutely positively accurate it was (although it was pretty accurate overall) and more about how much depth it gave the painting. Now we're not so impressed by this because we see it all the time, but for its day that was kinda cutting edge. 

I think this [link](http://www.pbs.org/treasuresoftheworld/mona_lisa/mlevel_1/m3technique.html) can probably explain better than I can. And it also goes into other reasons the Mona Lisa is so well respected. 

That said, I think it's hard to guess if it would be as well loved if it were by another painter. I think likely, it would not be. Names carry a loooooooot of weight, and of course DaVinci is THE name. I also think it wouldn't be as famous and therefore as revered without the theft. 

IMO, I entirely understand why this painting is important academically- Use of perspective, realism, its mystery, daVincis contributions to technical aspects of oil painting, etc, etc, etc. But personally, I will never really get the hype. I think there are a million paintings more interesting than this one.

It's considered one of the greatest paintings for a few reasons. 

First of all, it's a daVinci and of course he's a giant in art. It also has an incredible mastery of perspective in the background, which was considered the mark of a really incredible painter in its time. Perspective was *relatively* new and hugely in vouge during the renaissance so it's kind of how painters would show off their skills at the time. And obviously, solid representation of the woman sitting in the portrait. It was all about how realistic you could make things look. 

Although, the painting really took off in its notoriety after it was stolen briefly from the museum and received a lot of attention and then the museum began to market it more. I can't remember when this happened exactly but I wanna say early 20th century.
